front: Michigan default BI liability limits (policies issued after July 1, 2020)

back: $50,000/$100,000. Requires signing the DIFS 'Michigan Choice of Bodily Injury Liability Coverage Limits' form; with no effective choice, 250/500 applies.

front: Failure to produce proof of insurance
back: Civil infraction. Electronic proof is OK. Proof shown to court before the appearance date: no fine, fee up to $25. Knowingly false proof: misdemeanor, up to 1 yr / $1,000.

front: Two policies with different PIP medical limits
back: No stacking: the total is capped at the highest single-policy limit.

front: PIP priority: employee in employer's vehicle
back: Insurer of the employer-furnished vehicle.

front: PIP priority: motorcyclist hit by a motor vehicle
back: 1) insurer of the vehicle's owner, 2) of the vehicle's operator, 3) motorcycle operator's auto insurer, 4) motorcycle owner's auto insurer.

After 55 days or on renewal: only for a final license suspension/revocation (nonpayment cancellations are outside Chapter 32). Notice: certified mail, at least 20 days; appeal within 7 days (no appeal for a cancellation in the first 55 days).

Chapter 32 (MCL 500.3204): a nonrenewal is not a "cancellation" if notice is mailed first-class at least 20 days before the termination date. Chapter 32 does not apply to nonpayment cancellations (3208, 3212). Separately, the Essential Insurance Act (MCL 500.2123) requires 30 days' written notice stating each specific reason for a "termination" of auto insurance (20 days within the first 55 days).
If the insurer requests non-OEM parts, the written estimate must identify each part with a disclosure in at least 10-point bold type.

Insurers must offer: Limited collision (no deductible; pays only if the operator was not more than 50% at fault) and Broad form (pays regardless of fault; deductible waived if not more than 50% at fault). Standard collision, and limited collision with a deductible, may also be offered. Rejection of both offered coverages must be in writing.
Liability/med pay/UM: ask within 14 days. Collision/OTC: 14 days if any declared auto has it; otherwise 4 days, and a $500 deductible applies to a loss that occurs before you ask.
Bail bond up to $250; loss of earnings up to $250/day; appeal/attachment bonds; post-judgment interest; all in addition to limits.
